evidence: task/task.toml:20-24 has [environment] build_timeout_sec = 600.0, network_mode = "public", cpus = 2, memory_mb = 4096 -- byte-identical to the template task.toml and to staged-task-contract.md lines 56-60; no docker_image and no allow_internet key anywhere in task.toml; no secret literal under [environment] (the only credential-shaped values are the frozen [verifier.env] ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY} template and empty ANTHROPIC_API_KEY at lines 34-35, which belong to the verifier block and are expected by the profile). network_mode = "public" is correct per the workbook text and SKILL delivery profile; the Internal sheet's older 'no-network' wording is superseded by the public profile and the current workbook row. environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the template Dockerfile (diff empty): node:22-bookworm-slim, express@5.1.0 + better-sqlite3@12.4.1 preinstalled globally with NODE_PATH, no ENV/ARG secrets. 'Nothing that secretly needs an install': solution/app/package.json depends only on express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1 and server.js requires only those plus node builtins (crypto, fs, path); solve.sh is a plain cp; integration.md:3 publicly states both modules are preinstalled. The only password in the environment is the documented demo 'password123' (walls-and-retention.md:3), a known false positive. Actual run: built the frozen environment/ image and ran it with --cpus 2 --memory 4096m: printed 'mods ok v22.23.2' (both modules resolve), /app contains only .git and .gitkeep with commit 'Initialize task workspace', /assets and /instructions are present and world-readable, and env contains no key/token/secret variables. Image removed afterward. 2 CPU / 4 GB is ample for an Express + better-sqlite3 app with no native compile needed at agent time. Adversarial angle: a broken app cannot exploit this row (pure environment wiring), and a conforming app needing nothing beyond the declared modules runs in the declared limits; public network means a model fetching extra npm packages is also not starved.
